rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, two-season field experiments (2004, 2005) at Citra FL with sensor-controlled drip irrigation of zucchini. Q2: Table 3 / Section 3.4, sensor-based treatments SUR1 and SDI (up to five short daily windows triggered by QIC capacitance probe) gave marketable yields of 27.6 and 26.9 Mg/ha vs 20.5 for the once-daily 2-h timed treatment; Section 3.3 attributes lower SUR1 yield in 2004 to water stress when supply fell below ETc. Q4: Fig. 2 and Section 3.4, TDR-measured volumetric water content at 0-0.3 m for each scheduling treatment, and cumulative irrigation vs calculated ETc (Fig. 1A), used to explain water stress and yield differences. Q8: Section 3.1, three unprotected frost events in 2005 reduced harvests, growth and yield relative to 2004. Q9: Tables 2 and 3 report coefficients of variation for yield; Fig. 1 bars show 1 S.E.
rows.notes: Claim is phrased about irrigation scheduling generally; the study's scheduling is soil-moisture-sensor-based, so it matches the technology. Yield measured by harvest only (one method). Single site, one crop, sandy soil. Q7 borderline: authors say soil water availability was a primal component of yield and attribute SUR1 2004 yield loss to a too-dry set point, but do not state a threshold requirement for the yield effect; the field-capacity-threshold condition is stated for leaching only.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own field experiments. Q2: Fig. 1C and Section 3.4, sensor-controlled SDI leached 1.7-2.4 kg/ha NO3-N vs 35-45 kg/ha under the timed treatment and 20-26 under the wetter sensor set point; Abstract and Conclusions state sensor control reduced irrigation and minimized N leaching. Q3: Section 2.2, leaching assessed by zero-tension drainage lysimeters (Fig. 1B-C) and independently by soil coring at three depths showing N displacement in the profile (Fig. 4, Section 3.4). Q4: Fig. 1B and Section 3.4, drainage volume measured (62 mm for SUR2/SURtime vs 14 mm for SDI) and TDR soil water fluctuations linked to percolation below the root zone. Q7: Conclusions, sensor-based irrigation reduces leaching when soil volumetric water content is kept within the field capacity threshold. Q9: Fig. 1C bars represent 1 S.E. of cumulative NO3-N leaching; soil solution nitrate given as mean +/- SD.
rows.notes: Single site, sandy soil, one crop, plot scale. Q8: text notes SUR1 drainage was not monitored (Fig. 1 caption) and rainfall contribution assumed negligible, but these are not framed as limitations of the leaching result, so answered no.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own field experiments 2004-2005. Q2: Table 3 Study 3, SUR1 (sensor) yield 27.6 vs SURtime 20.5 Mg/ha (+35%), IWUE 16.1 vs 4.3 kg/m3 (+274%), NUE 37.1 vs 26.5% (+40%); SURtime described as one fixed 2-h daily event mimicking grower practice. Q4: Fig. 2 and Section 3.4, measured VWC dynamics and irrigation vs ETc (Fig. 1A), plus soil nitrate profiles (Fig. 4) showing N displacement under high-volume irrigation decreasing dry matter and N accumulation. Q8: Section 3.1, frosts in 2005 reduced harvest events, growth and yield. Q9: Table 3 coefficients of variation for yield, IWUE and NUE.
rows.notes: Percentages in the passage match Table 3 Study 3 exactly. Yield by harvest only; one site and crop.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own field experiments. Q2: Table 1 and Conclusions, sensor-based treatments applied 160-329 mm vs 482 mm for the timed treatment, a 33-80% reduction in irrigation; Table 3, IWUE 16.1 vs 4.3 kg/m3. Q4: Fig. 2 (TDR soil water content showing fewer fluctuations under sensor control), Fig. 1A (irrigation vs calculated ETc) and Fig. 1B (drainage volumes) measured as the pathway by which sensor control saves water. Q9: Table 3 C.V. for IWUE; Fig. 1A bars show 1 S.E. for cumulative irrigation.
rows.notes: Water applied measured by flowmeters only (single method). No condition stated as a requirement for the water saving itself; the field-capacity-threshold condition concerns leaching. Frost limitation concerns yield rather than water applied.

Q4: Fig. 2 measured VWC, Fig. 1A irrigation vs ETc, Fig. 1B drainage volumes. Q9: Table 3 C.V.; Fig. 1A bars 1 S.E.
rows.notes: Study matches the claim (capacitance sensors, drip, zucchini, small plots). Single method for water use, one site, no requirement stated for the water saving.
